# ferentin_mcp_scope_defaults (Resource)

MCP scope defaults: what a local MCP server or tool on a managed device meets when **no MCP policy applies to it**, for the tenant default or for one device group. Four defaults, each enforced or rehearsed (`report_only`):

* **server approval** — a local MCP server config that is not approved
* **remote entry** — a remote MCP server entry that is not approved; it equals server approval until devices carry the two apart, so it is read-only here
* **unattributed** — a local MCP server started by a process the device cannot place in an identified AI agent's session (for example from Terminal.app)
* **tool vetting** — an unvetted tool on an approved local server: its mode, the action per risk rating, and the approval routing an `ask_*` tier needs

It also holds the **agent evidence floor**: how strongly a device must have verified the AI agent before a local MCP policy that grants on that agent applies.

Omit `device_group_id` for the **tenant default**, which every device without a group default of its own runs. Set it for one device group.

Each default is sent only when it is in the config: one left out keeps what the tenant has, so a default can stay with the admin console.

~> **This resource writes the endpoint posture row.** The platform stores these defaults on the same row `ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings` manages for the scope, so the two share one version. When an apply changes both, the provider retries a write the other made stale, as long as the defaults this resource sends were not changed elsewhere. On a device group with no posture of its own, the first write here creates the group's row as a copy of the tenant default's posture. Destroying a group's `ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings` deletes that row, and with it the group's own scope defaults: the group then runs the tenant's, and the next plan here shows the difference. Where MCP policies have replaced endpoint MCP rules, the platform refuses that delete while the group's defaults differ from the tenant's, and the settings resource leaves the row in force with a warning; deleting the device group still removes it. When both resources manage one group, make this one `depends_on` the settings resource so the group row is created once.

~> **Destroy does not reset anything.** The platform has no way to delete the defaults, and resetting them to the permissive built-ins would stand enforcement down silently, so `terraform destroy` (or removing the block) drops the resource from state and leaves the defaults in force, with a warning. To stand them down, apply `report_only` values first.

## Import

```
terraform import ferentin_mcp_scope_defaults.tenant <tenant_id>
terraform import ferentin_mcp_scope_defaults.contractors <tenant_id>/<device_group_id>
```

The `import_id` of each row of `ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings_scopes` works here too.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# MCP scope defaults: what a local MCP server or tool meets when no MCP policy
# applies to it. Omit device_group_id for the tenant default; set it for one
# device group.
#
# Each default is sent only when it is set here; one left out keeps what the
# tenant has. A default's mode is `enforce`, or `report_only` to rehearse it:
# devices act as if it were report_only and the platform records what it would
# have refused. Unset, the mode is enforce for a value that refuses.
#
# NOTE: these defaults live on the scope's endpoint posture row, the same row
# ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings writes. `terraform destroy` leaves them in
# force (the platform cannot delete them); apply report_only values first to
# stand them down.

# The device group the second block targets. Declared here so the snippet
# stands on its own; see ferentin_device_group for the full resource.
resource "ferentin_device_group" "contractors" {
  name   = "contractors"
  source = "manual"
}

# Tenant default: observe first. Rehearse quarantining unapproved local MCP
# servers, and record what blocking unattributed ones would refuse.
resource "ferentin_mcp_scope_defaults" "tenant" {
  server_approval      = "quarantine"
  server_approval_mode = "report_only"

  unattributed      = "block"
  unattributed_mode = "report_only"

  # Unvetted tools on approved local servers, by risk rating. An ask_once /
  # ask_every_call tier needs approval routing.
  tool_vetting_mode = "enforce"
  tool_vetting_risk_policy = {
    low    = "allow"
    medium = "ask_once"
    high   = "deny"
  }
  tool_vetting_approval_config = jsonencode({
    step_up_mode    = "approve"
    timeout_seconds = 900
    channels        = [{ type = "invocation_context" }]
  })

  # Credit a ferentin_mcp_policy grant that names an AI agent (subject.agents)
  # on a local server only when the device verified the agent's code
  # signature. Off by default, which credits no such grant. A deny naming an
  # agent applies whatever this says.
  agent_evidence_floor = "lineage_signature"
}

# Contractors: enforce. Tool vetting follows the tenant default's.
resource "ferentin_mcp_scope_defaults" "contractors" {
  device_group_id = ferentin_device_group.contractors.group_id

  server_approval   = "block"
  unattributed      = "block"
  tool_vetting_mode = "inherit"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `agent_evidence_floor` (String) The weakest device-verified agent evidence at which a grant on a local MCP server that names an AI agent (`ferentin_mcp_policy` with `effect` `allow` or `step_up` and `subject.agents` or `subject.agent_evidence`) is credited:

* `off` — no grant on the agent is credited; the default
* `lineage_name` — the agent's process name in the MCP shim's lineage
* `lineage_signature` — its kernel-verified code signature, which is what every agent a device verifies reads as today
* `hook_correlated` — also matched to the agent's own pre-tool hook; no device reports it yet

A deny naming an agent applies at any level, whatever this says. The platform decides it where a local server starts and at its tool calls; devices do not receive it. On a device group, `inherit` follows the tenant default's, and is what a group that sets none reads as. Omit to keep the current value.
- `device_group_id` (String) Device group these defaults apply to — reference `ferentin_device_group.<name>.group_id`. Omit for the tenant default. Part of the resource's identity: changing it forces replacement.
- `server_approval` (String) What a device does with a local MCP server config that no policy applies to and that is not approved:

* `report_only` — report it, change nothing on the machine
* `quarantine` — move the offending config aside so the client cannot load it (the entry is preserved in a root-owned sidecar first)
* `block` — block the server's traffic outright (needs the NetworkExtension content filter)

Omit to keep the current value.
- `server_approval_mode` (String) `enforce`, or `report_only` to rehearse `server_approval`: devices act as if it were `report_only` and the platform records what the value would have refused. Unset, it is `report_only` when `server_approval` is `report_only` and `enforce` otherwise, so setting a refusing value alone enforces it. `enforce` is refused with `report_only` (it refuses nothing). Only set together with `server_approval`.
- `tenant_id` (String)
- `tool_vetting_approval_config` (String) Approval routing for step-up approvals raised by unvetted local MCP tools, as JSON — write it with `jsonencode({...})`. The object is the platform's approval config: `step_up_mode` (`reauth` / `approve`), `channels` (at least one; `type` is `invocation_context`, `slack`, `email`, `webhook` or `approver_dm`), and optionally `approver_role`, `timeout_seconds`, `escalation`, `context_fields`, `redacted_fields` and the risk bounds. On a device group it is the group's own; null means the group follows the tenant default's.

A key this provider version does not know fails at plan rather than being dropped. A formatting difference from the platform's stored form is not drift. Omit to keep the current config. Clearing it is done in the admin console: `{}` is refused here.
- `tool_vetting_mode` (String) What an unvetted tool on an approved local MCP server meets: `enforce` (the risk policy decides), or `report_only` to let it run and record what the risk policy would have answered. `report_only` round-trips every call to the platform and lifts the approved-server gate on allow tiers, so it is a rehearsal, not a setting to leave on; an admin's vetting denial, the schema-flap breaker, the tool cap and data protection still apply. On a device group, `inherit` follows the tenant default's, and is what a group that sets none reads as. Omit to keep the current value.
- `tool_vetting_risk_policy` (Object) What an unvetted local MCP tool gets at each risk rating: an object with `low`, `medium` and `high`, each one of `allow`, `ask_once`, `ask_every_call` or `deny`. All three are required. Unset on the platform is the legacy behaviour (step up when approval routing exists, deny otherwise). On a device group it is the group's own policy; null means the group follows the tenant default's.

~> Any `ask_*` tier needs approval routing with at least one channel (`tool_vetting_approval_config`, or on a device group the tenant default's), or the platform refuses the write.

Omit to keep the current policy. Clearing it (on a group, returning to the tenant's) is done in the admin console. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tool_vetting_risk_policy))
- `unattributed` (String) What a device does with a local MCP server started by a process it cannot place in an identified AI agent's session: `report_only` (start it and record it as `agent_unattributed`) or `block` (refuse it). Agents the device cannot verify, such as Gemini CLI, read as unattributed when started outside another agent, so review the recorded `agent_unattributed` admissions (or rehearse with `unattributed_mode = "report_only"`) before blocking. Only devices on an agent build that reads it enforce `block`. Omit to keep the current value.
- `unattributed_mode` (String) `enforce`, or `report_only` to rehearse `unattributed`: devices act as if it were `report_only` and the platform records what the value would have refused. Unset, it is `report_only` when `unattributed` is `report_only` and `enforce` otherwise, so setting a refusing value alone enforces it. `enforce` is refused with `report_only` (it refuses nothing). Only set together with `unattributed`.

### Read-Only

- `agent_evidence_floor_source` (String) Read-only. Where the agent evidence floor in force comes from: `device_group`, `tenant` or `built_in` (none set, which is `off`).
- `id` (String) `<tenant_id>` for the tenant default, `<tenant_id>/<device_group_id>` for a group.
- `remote_entry` (String) Read-only. The remote entry default, which equals `server_approval` until devices carry them apart.
- `remote_entry_mode` (String) Read-only. The remote entry default's mode.
- `source` (String) Read-only. Where `server_approval`, `remote_entry` and `unattributed` come from: `device_group` (this group's own posture), `tenant` (the tenant default's, for a group with no posture of its own) or `built_in` (no posture at all).
- `tool_vetting_approval_config_source` (String) Read-only. Where the approval routing in force comes from: `device_group`, `tenant` or `built_in`.
- `tool_vetting_mode_source` (String) Read-only. Where the tool vetting mode in force comes from: `device_group`, `tenant` or `built_in`.
- `tool_vetting_risk_policy_source` (String) Read-only. Where the risk policy in force comes from: `device_group`, `tenant` or `built_in`.
- `version` (Number) The scope's posture row version, sent as `If-Match`. Shared with `ferentin_endpoint_policy_settings` for the same scope. Null while a device group has no posture of its own; the first write then sends no `If-Match`.
